bumbuna-hydro-reservoir-resettlement.whole: The 2005 appraisal document put the plant at 50 MW installed power, with average output of 315 GWh a year. The plant was commissioned on 6 November 2009, and the Bank's completion report says it has not run at that level: the shaft of generating unit 2 cracked in November 2012 and the unit stopped working, and unit 1 ran at 8 to 10 MW, then at 22 to 23 MW against a rated 25 MW after its shaft was replaced in April 2013. A target of raising electricity sales from 68.9 GWh in 2003 to 230 GWh in 2008 was recorded as not monitored; the project also established the Loma Mountains National Park, of 33,201 hectares, in December 2012. No economic rate of return was calculated at appraisal or at completion. The completion report rated the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Unsatisfactory and efficiency low; the Independent Evaluation Group rated the outcome Unsatisfactory, Bank performance Unsatisfactory and efficiency Negligible. These are the lender's own figures; no independent count of the plant's output was found.

kawanda-masaka-line-galatiya.whole: The 137 km double-circuit 220 kV line between the Kawanda and Masaka substations became operational in December 2018, with a new Masaka substation working from June 2018, by the Bank's own account. Electricity flowing through the Masaka substation rose from 381 GWh to 605 GWh against a target of 617.4 GWh, and the Bank counts 52,084 households given new or improved service against a target of 16,500, 5,447 new community connections against 8,000, and 34,044 people given access against 50,000. The economic rate of return was worked out for the transmission line component alone, 83 per cent of project cost at appraisal and 79 per cent at completion, and counts reductions in unmet demand, added capacity to meet demand, lower transmission losses and savings in repairs and maintenance: it was 22.2 per cent at appraisal and 32.6 per cent at completion. The Independent Evaluation Group says the rise came mainly from the project costing US$81.8 million against the appraisal estimate of US$147.6 million, and that a large part of that saving was unplanned, from steep falls in world steel and aluminium prices. Both the Bank and the Evaluation Group rated the outcome Moderately Satisfactory and efficiency Modest; the Bank rated the relevance of the objectives High and the Evaluation Group Substantial. The figures are the lender's and UETCL's own; no independent measurement was found.

kibera-mukuru-railway-relocation.whole: The relocation was one part of a four-country project whose main business was customs and transport. By the Bank's own count the time a standard container spent at Mombasa fell from 13 days in 2005 to three days in 2014, and at Dar es Salaam from 18 days to seven, while crossing time at the Malaba border between Kenya and Uganda fell from 45 hours to 2.1 hours by September 2015; of twelve one-stop border posts the Independent Evaluation Group says appear to have been planned, it found five half-built at closing and two not started. On the railway, the target of cutting Mombasa to Kampala transit from 14 days to seven was not met, nor the target of raising rail's share of Northern Corridor freight from 16 to 30 per cent, and the Evaluation Group records that the concessionaire invested US$139 million between 2011 and 2015 while reporting losses of more than 10 per cent of revenue every year from 2011. The appraisal economic rate of return, which counted savings in time and in uncertainty, was 26 per cent, and 49 per cent for the railway component, most of that from government concession fees; that analysis covered US$118.36 million of cost, which the review's text calls 60 per cent of the project cost estimated at appraisal and its own data table 42 per cent, and no rate was calculated at completion. The Bank rated the outcome Moderately Satisfactory and the Evaluation Group Moderately Unsatisfactory, and the risk to the outcome Substantial where the Bank rated it Modest. The figures are the lender's own; no independent check of them was found.

kisip-informal-settlements-fatalities.whole: By the Bank's own count the project upgraded 98.28 km of roads to bitumen standard against a target of 90 km, rehabilitated 120 km of footpaths, laid 59 km of sewers with 4,788 sewer connections, provided 8,739 new piped household water connections against a target of 7,306, and installed 21 ablution blocks, 11 water kiosks and 134 high-mast lights. Tenure security was recorded in 80 settlements against a target of 86, and about 7,300 title deeds were issued or sent to counties by closing. A survey the project commissioned put the number of people who benefited at 1,389,980 against a target of 1,030,000, and the number with improved tenure security at 125,525 against a revised target of 100,000 and an original target of 180,000; the project recorded 26,148 jobs on construction sites. An economic analysis done only at closing, covering 76 per cent of actual cost, counted travel time and vehicle cost savings, better access to jobs and services, fewer days lost to flooding, less property damage and health gains, and put the internal rate of return at 41.4 per cent for roads and drainage, 41.2 per cent for water and sanitation and 30 per cent for the floodlights; the Evaluation Group's data table gives one rate for that analysis, 38 per cent. Both the Bank and the Evaluation Group rated the outcome Satisfactory, and the Evaluation Group rated efficiency Substantial. Every figure comes from the lender or a survey it commissioned; no independent check was found.

lower-nzoia-irrigation-unpaid-compensati.whole: By the Bank's own count the scheme gave 2,457 hectares new or improved irrigation and drainage, which the Independent Evaluation Group puts at 79 per cent of the revised target of 3,095 hectares, against an original target of 4,043 hectares, and reached 8,142 farmers against a revised target of 11,133. The project built 34 km of flood dykes, a target cut from 44 km, and counts 66,700 people with increased flood protection; produce marketed from the scheme was worth US$7.3 million against a target of 2,683 million Kenyan shillings, about US$30 million. The economic rate of return was 14.6 per cent at appraisal, counting gains in crop yields and market value over 20 years at a 12 per cent discount rate, and 13.81 per cent at closing, worked out over 30 years at a 6 per cent discount rate, so the two rates rest on different assumptions; the review also records re-estimates of 13.8 per cent at the 2015 additional financing, 8.9 per cent when US$70 million was cancelled in 2019 and 24.61 per cent at the 2023 additional financing. The review records that 85 to 90 per cent of the project's new or upgraded monitoring stations stopped working about one and a half to two years after installation for want of maintenance money, so the flood forecasting and early warning system they fed could no longer function, and that the government undertook to finish the remaining 22 per cent of the irrigation scheme from its own budget. Both the Bank and the Evaluation Group rated the outcome Moderately Satisfactory and efficiency Modest. The figures are the lender's own; no independent check of them was found.

rsdp-apl3-road-deaths.whole: By the Bank's own count 498 km of federal trunk and link road were upgraded against a target of 509 km, and the construction work provided 5,764 jobs, about 13 per cent of them held by women. The share of the road network in good or fair condition rose from 70 per cent in 2006 to 91 per cent in 2014 against a target of 82 per cent. Traffic in 2015, after the roads opened, was 174 per cent higher on the Aposto to Irba Moda to Negele road, 123 per cent higher from Gedo through Bako to Nekempte and 299 per cent higher from Gondar to Debark, and road fund revenue rose from 258.2 million birr in 2006 to 1,200 million birr in 2014 against a target of 1,075 million. The economic rate of return, which counts savings in vehicle operating costs and travel time and covered 93 per cent of project cost at appraisal and 94 per cent afterwards, was 16.5 per cent at appraisal and 27.1 per cent afterwards, a rise the Independent Evaluation Group attributes mainly to traffic growing faster than the 7 per cent a year assumed; contracts ran on average 151 per cent over time and about 12.4 per cent over cost. Both bodies rated the outcome Moderately Satisfactory and Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory, but the Evaluation Group rated borrower performance Moderately Unsatisfactory where the completion report rated it Moderately Satisfactory. The figures are the lender's own; no independent check of them was found.

uganda-ert2-grid-compensation.whole: By the Bank's own count the project connected 97,753 households against an original target of 109,000 and a revised target of 120,000, and gave 643,674 people access to electricity against a target of 720,000. It electrified 522 health centres against a target of 464, 546 rural schools against 560, and 44 water supply schemes, up from 15; households using solar panels rose from 12,000 to 23,000 against a target of 32,000, and no connections at all were made through independent small grids, against a target of 5,300. The share of the rural population with electricity in the project areas rose from 4 to 7 per cent; the Independent Evaluation Group says the 7 per cent target was itself set from a Uganda Bureau of Statistics survey and that the rise in rural electrification cannot be fully attributed to the project. A second objective, increasing access to information and communication technology in rural Uganda, drew no activity at all, which the Evaluation Group rated Negligible. An economic rate of return of 12 per cent was calculated only at closing, for two of the project's three components, counting avoided diesel and kerosene costs, avoided peak load demand and energy savings. The Evaluation Group rated the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory where the completion report rated it Moderately Satisfactory, and rated efficiency Modest where the completion report rated it Substantial. The figures are the lender's own; no independent check of them was found.

upper-cisokan-pumped-storage-land.whole: The loan was for 1,040 MW of pumped storage peaking capacity for the Java-Bali power system, and the Bank records the increase in peaking capacity as zero. A dispute with the main civil works contractor over access to the site, after a landslide, took from 2016 to 2021 to resolve, and the contracts already procured could not be awarded while it ran. What was delivered was the access road, the procurement of the main construction contracts, which came in up to 25 per cent below estimate and were carried over to a later loan, and a feasibility study for a second scheme, the Matenggeng pumped storage project, completed in July 2018. At the December 2018 restructuring the Bank counted 65 per cent of the affected households as having restored or increased incomes or assets against a target of 100 per cent, with livelihood capacity built in 22 per cent of the villages. The appraisal cost-benefit analysis, covering 84 per cent of project cost, gave an economic rate of return of 19 per cent and a financial rate of return of 16 per cent; neither was recalculated at completion. Both the Bank and the Independent Evaluation Group rated the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory and efficiency Modest. The figures are the lender's and PLN's own; no independent check of them was found.
